newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, Bell plan civilian tilt-rotor aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, Bell plan civilian tilt-rotor aircraft.

text.p: Boeing Co. and Textron Inc.'s Bell Helicopter division Monday will announce plans to build a civilian version of the military's V-22 Osprey tilt-rotor aircraft, an executive said.
Boeing defense and space President Jerry King said the Bell Boeing 609 will be available in 2001 at an estimated price of $8 million to $10 million.

The two-engine aircraft, which will have the ability to take off and land like a helicopter but fly nearly twice as fast, will carry up to nine passengers and will be targeted at executives in industries such as oil exploration.
"A number of customers have expressed very strong interest," King told reporters at a news conference to discuss the Pentagon's award of a fighter jet contract.
He said the Bell Boeing partnership would build three prototypes of the tilt-rotor craft by 1999 and then seek U.S. Federal Aviation Administration certification.

The V-22 features a unique design of two turboprop engines that thrust vertically on takeoff and landing but then swing back to provide horizontal thrust for a cruise speed of some 250 mph. The Pentagon has agreed to buy 523 of the tilt-rotor craft over the next 25 years for an estimated $36 billion.
